# The Dust That Blazes

## Scripture

*"For he knows how we are formed, he remembers that we are dust."* — Psalm 103:14 (NIV)

## Reflection

On any clear November night, you might catch a Taurid or Leonid meteor—a brief streak of light across the darkness. What you're seeing is tiny. Most meteoroids are no larger than a grain of sand. A speck of dust, heated white-hot by its plunge through our atmosphere, blazing brighter than the stars around it.

The psalmist says God remembers we are dust. Not with disappointment—with tenderness. He knows how we are formed. He remembers the dust.

Here is the strange glory of it: God does not despise dust. He lifts it. He sets it burning. A grain of sand can streak across the sky and make someone stop and look up. So can a life surrendered to Him—small, ordinary, formed from the same stuff as the ground beneath our feet—yet capable of a flash of light that points beyond itself.

This fall, when a meteor scratches its bright arc across the dark, let it remind you: God is not waiting for you to become something other than dust before He uses you. He knows exactly what you are made of. He made you that way on purpose. And in His hands, dust catches fire.

## Prayer

Lord, You remember that we are dust—and still You call us to shine. Thank You for knowing us completely and loving us anyway. Take our small, ordinary lives and set them burning with Your light, that others might look up and see You. In Jesus' name, amen.
